analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, covering historical release notes (v0.9.x and earlier, roughly lines 4069-4530). The file_changes patch shows only the head range 11-39 as changed (a new v0.10.10 candidate section: waitlists, `darkbloom waitlist`, approval gating for new sandbox setup and new cluster pairing). That changed range is not within the supplied text units, so I could only see the patch excerpt, which is truncated. The supplied units are unchanged surrounding historical documentation.

I found no executable code, configuration or security-control changes in the supplied text. Statements such as App Attest recovery, APNs diagnostics, and encrypted SSD prefix cache defaults describe prior releases and are consistent with the canonical threat model (T-041/SEC-035 30-minute TTL, HMAC-keyed names, T-053/T-054 fencing). I did not verify those claims against source.

Remaining integration questions: the new v0.10.10 waitlist gating (TB-013 sandbox setup, TB-014/cluster pairing) depends on coordinator and CLI code outside this batch. Whether an unreachable, unauthenticated, or fail-open coordinator response can bypass approval, and whether the `--yes` flag or the grandfathering of existing setups opens a new attack surface, cannot be judged from the changelog alone. The patch says that when the coordinator does not offer waitlists yet, both new setups proceed as before, which is a fail-open design that the code reviewers should confirm is intentional and limited to the absence of the feature, not to errors. This is a documentation-level note, not a finding, since no code was supplied.
